name: BaroEase
tagline: Migraine tracker with barometric pressure alerts. Your health data lives on your device; an account is optional.
overview: This Privacy Policy describes how {{app}} handles information when you use the app. It applies to every version of {{app}} distributed by {{publisher}} on the app stores listed above.

{{app}} is a migraine tracker for people whose attacks may be linked to barometric-pressure changes. It is built local-first: your attacks, symptoms, notes, medications, reminders and notification history are stored on your device, an account is optional, and logging an attack works with no network at all. If you never sign in, we never receive any of it.

Signing in with Google or Apple turns on cross-device sync. There is no separate switch — the sign-in screen tells you this beforehand. Your attacks, medications, reminders and notification history are then uploaded as encrypted payloads. Two things travel with each record in readable form, because sync cannot work without them: which account owns it, and when it was last changed. Neither says anything about what is in the record. Exports never sync; they stay on the device that made them.

Important — this is encryption, but it is not end-to-end encryption. The key for your account is generated and held by our backend, so that a new device of yours can be given it after you sign in. That means Google's infrastructure, which hosts our backend, is technically able to decrypt these payloads. We do not read them and nothing in the app is designed to, but we will not tell you that only you can read them, because that would not be true.

If you grant permission, {{app}} reads your sleep and your step count from Apple Health, read-only. These are two separate permissions with two separate switches — allowing one does not allow the other. The analysis runs on your device. We never write to Apple Health, never store what we read in our own database, and never upload it, not even when you are signed in and sync is running.

{{app}} uses Firebase Crashlytics and Firebase Analytics. Analytics records actions, never content: that an attack was logged, that the paywall was opened, that an export was shared. It never carries intensity, head location, medication names, attack times or coordinates. While you are signed in, both are tagged with your account identifier — an opaque ID, not your name or email — so a crash can be traced to one account. Signing out clears it.

You can export everything from Settings as JSON, CSV or a PDF doctor report. Past exports are kept in the app so you can re-share them, and are full copies of your data. There are then two separate destructive actions. "Delete all data" wipes the local database and those export files, deletes your synced records and backend alert record, and gives up your push token, coarse location and threshold — but keeps your account, so your subscription binding survives. "Delete account" is the whole teardown: synced records, account record, encryption key, then the login itself. Neither cancels your subscription; that lives in the App Store and only you can cancel it there.

{{app}} is not directed at children under 16 and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, contact {{email}} and we will delete it.

Medical disclaimer: {{app}} is a self-tracking tool. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition. Always consult a qualified clinician about your health.
If anything here is unclear, email {{email}} before you continue using the app.
summary: Your attacks, medications and notes are stored on your device. Without an account, we never receive them.
Signing in is optional and turns on encrypted cross-device sync. The key is held by our backend, so this is not end-to-end encryption.
Apple Health sleep and step data is read on-device only and is never uploaded.
Location is only requested While Using the app and at reduced accuracy, stored as a ~5 km area, never as coordinates.

items: Attack logs — intensity, head location, time, physical exertion
Weather snapshot attached to each attack
collects.purpose: This is what the app is for. It is stored locally and, if you are not signed in, we never receive it.

items: Encrypted attack, medication, reminder and notification payloads
Account identifier and last-changed timestamp, stored unencrypted alongside each payload
collects.purpose: Sync your history across your devices. Signing in turns this on; there is no separate switch. Payloads are encrypted, but the key is held by our backend, so this is not end-to-end encryption.

items: A 5-character geohash — an area of roughly 5 km
collects.purpose: Group nearby users into a single weather-forecast lookup and decide whether a pressure drop is coming. Precise coordinates are never requested or stored.
Decide when a pressure alert is warranted and deliver it to your device. Stored against a random device identifier when you have no account.
Authenticate you and show you which account you are signed in to. Only collected if you choose to sign in with Google or Apple.
Identify and fix crashes and performance problems. Tagged with your opaque account identifier while you are signed in.

items: Actions taken in the app — for example that an attack was logged, that the paywall was opened, that an export was shared
collects.purpose: Understand which features are used so the app can be improved. Records that something happened, never its content: no intensity, head location, medication name, attack time or location ever becomes an analytics parameter.

Photos or media from your device

permissions.name: Location (While Using, reduced accuracy)
permissions.reason: Attach a weather snapshot to an attack and work out whether a pressure drop is coming. "Always" access is never requested. Deny it and the app still works; pressure alerts do not.

permissions.name: Notifications
permissions.reason: Deliver the medication reminders you schedule and the pressure alerts you switch on.

permissions.name: Apple Health — Sleep
permissions.reason: Read your sleep, on-device only, to look for a correlation with your attacks. A separate permission from step count.

permissions.name: Apple Health — Steps
permissions.reason: Read your step count, on-device only, to look for a correlation with your attacks. A separate permission from sleep.

thirdParties.name: Google Firebase
thirdParties.purpose: Authentication, the alert record, encrypted sync payloads, push delivery and backend functions. Hosted in the European Union (europe-west1).

thirdParties.name: Firebase Analytics
thirdParties.purpose: Usage analytics — which features are used, never what you logged.

thirdParties.name: RevenueCat
thirdParties.purpose: Subscription and entitlement state. Card details are handled by Apple and never reach us.

thirdParties.name: Open-Meteo
thirdParties.purpose: Weather forecasts for a coarse location. No identifier or health data is sent.

thirdParties.name: Apple (Sign in with Apple, App Store, WeatherKit)
thirdParties.purpose: Optional sign-in, purchase processing, and weather forecasts.
